messages:
alex (platform): :rotating_light: Hosted API p95/p99 blowing up in us-west-2, queue growth noticed ~30m ago, now sustained. GPU pools showing 100% utilization and autoscaler failing to create new instances
incident-bot: [ALERT] hosted-api-us-west2 queue depth > 10k, p99 latency 18s, action: page oncall
meera (sre-oncall): on it. grabbing logs and checking autoscaler events
jun (runtime): I can pull runtime logs and check KV cache pressure. any customer-facing throttles yet?
alex (platform): support reported timeouts on some customers, getting a list from emily
emily (support): 3 customers flagged: AcmeCorp, Chatly, NoteFlow. They're seeing 504s and retry storms. I flagged priority and started support DM thread with stake holders
meera (sre-oncall): autoscaler logs show repeated `ProvisionerCreateError: quotaExceeded` around 6001234300..6001234400. also seeing `rate limit` errors from cloud provider when creating GPU instances
jun (runtime): that explains it. our fallback route to smaller model variants didn't kick — looks like routing policy failed during capacity check. investigating policy decision logs
ops-bot: current hosted-gpu-pool-uswest capacity: total_gpus=320, used_gpus=320, pending_provision=0. autoscaler_attempts=12, failed_attempts=12
alex (platform): can we temporarily throttle non-critical customers / lower batch sizes? want to protect core latency for paying customers
meera (sre-oncall): yes. immediate mitigation steps I'll run: 1) enable admission-control rate limit to 50rps for anonymous/self-serve tenants 2) set model-routing fallback to CPU-light path for best-effort requests 3) trigger manual provision retry with backoff
jun (runtime): adding: reduce batch_max_tokens from 4096->2048 for in-flight queues to free up buffer memory. applying now:

```
# runtime config patch
route: hosted-api/*
batching:
  max_tokens: 2048
  max_batch_size: 8
```

meera (sre-oncall): applying admission control: `rictl rate-limit set --tenant-type self-serve --limit 50 --region us-west-2`
ops-bot: admission control applied. non-paid traffic will be throttled.
jun (runtime): patched batching config deployed to routing layer. watch p95/p99 for next 2 mins
alex (platform): trying a manual provision to bypass autoscaler: `rictl provision --pool hosted-gpu-pool-uswest --size gpu-a100 --count 8 --force`
deploy-bot: manual provision request accepted, creating instances (req id 3f9c2)…
incident-bot: paging notification sent to escalation channel and oncall-assist (meera, jun)
meera (sre-oncall): autoscaler failures are due to cloud quota and provisioning rate-limits. I've submitted quota increase request but cloud response ETA is unknown. manual provision is best-effort
jun (runtime): runtime metrics: KV cache hit ratio dropping, memory pressure on models 7/8. if we can add the 8x GPUs we get some relief and avoid full fallback to CPU
meera (sre-oncall): manual provision succeeded partially — 4 instances created, 4 failed with `rate limit exceeded`. current used_gpus=324/328 (report)
ops-bot: updated counts: total_gpus=328, used_gpus=324, pending_provision=0
emily (support): summarizing customer impact to communicate: p95 up from 220ms->3.1s, p99 from 1.1s->19s for hosted API in us-west-2. Several 504s reported. prepping status page draft
taylor (product): prioritize paid tenants — can we move paid customer routing to dedicated pool in another region as fallback?
jun (runtime): cross-region live migration adds 200-400ms added latency but better than 20s p99. we can route top 5 paying tenants to eu-west-1 dedicated fallback pool temporarily
meera (sre-oncall): doing that now. updating routing policy to prefer `dedicated-eu-west-1` for tenants [AcmeCorp, Chatly, NoteFlow, Vaultly, SourcePad]

```
# routing command
rictl route update --tenant AcmeCorp --fallback dedicated-eu-west-1 --force
```

ops-bot: routing changes applied for 5 tenants. traffic shift in progress (~30s to observe).
meera (sre-oncall): after throttles, batching changes and partial manual provision, p95 dropped to 1.0s and p99 to 6.5s for us-west2 - still elevated but improved. queue depth reduced from 11k->4.2k
jun (runtime): runtime now reporting fewer OOMs and KV eviction rate stabilized. still seeing spike windows from some clients doing aggressive retries
emily (support): sent interim customer note: "We're aware of elevated errors and latencies in us-west. We're routing affected premium traffic to a fallback and throttling non-critical workloads. We'll update in 30m."
alex (platform): good. need an incident owner and whether this is Sev2 or Sev1. I'm leaning Sev2 but with customer-impacting 504s
meera (sre-oncall): assigning Sev2 for now. I'll take incident lead, jun is technical lead, alex will coordinate comms. escalation to Sev1 if more customers hit or p99 > 10s after next remediation window
jun (runtime): finding a bug in autoscaler backoff circuit — when we get repeated rate-limit errors the autoscaler marks the pool as unhealthy and stops retrying for 15m. file: `autoscaler/backoff_manager.go` line ~214. I'll push a hotfix to reduce exile to 60s for rate-limit cases\
alex (platform): can you prepare a safe rollout? we can do canary in us-west with 10% traffic after patch
jun (runtime): coding patch now. patch will be tested in staging then manual canary. ETA 25m to 1st canary
meera (sre-oncall): continuing mitigation: 1) keep throttles 2) watch queue drop 3) keep premium routing to fallback 4) continue manual provision attempts with lower concurrency
incident-bot: escalation: night-oncall will be paged in 20m for handoff unless cleared
emily (support): customers updated. internal CC: sales, CSMs notified for affected accounts
meera (sre-oncall): prepping postmortem notes. initial impact window: 6001234200 - present. will collect timeline and estimated affected request counts
ajun? (jun misspell): (typing)
jun (runtime): pushing hotfix branch `autoscaler/shorten-rate-limit-exile` -> run tests -> deploying to canary cluster

```
# autoscaler config diff
- rate_limit_exile_seconds: 900
+ rate_limit_exile_seconds: 60
```

ops-bot: canary deploy started for autoscaler hotfix (canary id: can-77). monitoring for provisioning success on subsequent attempts
meera (sre-oncall): handoff plan: if p99 < 3s and queue < 1k in 30m we can close paged incident and continue follow-up. if not, escalate to SEV1 and call cloud accounts for quota escalation
alex (platform): I'll prepare a short root-cause blurb and coordinate exec notification if needed
jun (runtime): canary shows autoscaler successfully creating instances on rate-limit returns. two test retries succeeded (no exile). if this holds we should see improved provisioning in next 5-10m
ops-bot: observed provisioning successes after hotfix: +6 GPUs created at 6001234625, autoscaler_retry_count reset
meera (sre-oncall): p95 now 680ms, p99 2.1s in us-west-2. queue depth 870. continuing to monitor and will do 1hr postmortem capture
emily (support): updating customers: follow-up note to go out in 20m with mitigation summary and ETA for RCA
meera (sre-oncall): handing to morning oncall - @meera -> @jun for next 2 hours check. I'll remain on-call until full recovery verified.
alex (platform): thanks all. please add any running TODOs to the incident doc and I'll draft the status update for execs

:thumbsup:
